claims.claim: B has expressed certainty (or given advice) that A can get there in time if they take the less heavy route
claims.attribute: B stated confidence about the less heavy route allowing A to arrive in time

evidence.quote: Are you sure that I can get there in time if we take the less heavy route ?

claims.adjudication_reason: Turn 3 'Are you sure that I can get there in time if we take the less heavy route?' presupposes B has expressed certainty or given advice about timing via that route. A is questioning B's prior assurance.

claims.claim: B has informed A about an additional cost A must pay
claims.attribute: B communicated a price increase or additional fee to A

evidence.quote: How much more do I have to pay ?

claims.adjudication_reason: Turn 5 'How much more do I have to pay?' presupposes B has already informed A about an additional cost. 'How much more' implies prior disclosure of a charge.

claims.claim: B is a driver providing paid transport service to A
claims.attribute: B is a paid transport driver (e.g., taxi/cab driver)

evidence.quote: if we take the less heavy route
How much more do I have to pay

claims.adjudication_reason: Combined evidence from Turn 3 ('if we take the less heavy route' — B controls route choice) and Turn 5 ('How much more do I have to pay' — paid service) strongly presupposes B is a driver providing paid transport.

claims.claim: B is in a position to choose or suggest an alternative route with less traffic
claims.attribute: B suggested or can take a less congested route

evidence.quote: if we take the less heavy route

claims.adjudication_reason: Turn 3 'if we take the less heavy route' presupposes B is in a position to choose or suggest routes. This is distinct from c3 (which infers the full driver/paid-service role) — c6 captures only the route-choice capacity.

claims.claim: B is the person A expects to transport them to their destination, as A directly asks B for an assessment of whether they can arrive in time
claims.attribute: B is the transport provider A relies on to reach the 11:30 train

evidence.quote: Do you think I can get there in time to catch the 11:30 train

claims.adjudication_reason: Turn 1 'Do you think I can get there in time to catch the 11:30 train?' directly addresses B for an assessment of arrival timing, presupposing B is the person expected to transport A. This is a minimal but valid presupposition distinct from the fuller c3 claim.
